title: LEVER: Adaptive Cost-Aware Proof Search Over AND/OR Graphs
title_zh: LEVER: 自适应成本感知证明搜索算法

paragraphs.en: Mathematicians value proofs for more than correctness: among correct proofs, simplicity, purity and the computational cost of finding them vary widely. Yet LLM-powered theorem provers largely search for any correct proof, and improve its quality only after it is found. We propose Lever , a proof search algorithm that makes the objective over correct proofs programmable and optimizes it during search . Lever scores partial proofs over an AND/OR proof graph, combining realized objective values with predictions for open subgoals, so the objective guides search before a proof is complete. The same mechanism optimizes computational cost, proof length, topical impurity, and even their weighted combinations, while the Lean kernel enforces correctness. On PutnamBench in Lean 4, under matched budgets, Lever costs 34 % 34\% less than a strong single-conversation agent while raising the solve rate from 80 % 80\% to 96 % 96\% . On reducing topical impurity, i.e. , how far a proof strays from its theorem’s subject, it improves over post-hoc refactoring ( 42 % 42\% reduction against 33 % 33\% ) at two-thirds of the cost and more reliably; on proof length, the metric refactoring is built for, it approaches refactoring. Varying the objective’s weights traces a quality–cost trade-off curve, so the user can choose how much a better proof is worth. Overall, Lever is a performant, cost-efficient and tunable proof search algorithm for navigating the space of correct proofs.
paragraphs.zh: 数学家重视证明的原因不仅在于其正确性：在正确的证明中，简洁性、纯粹性以及寻找这些证明的计算成本差异巨大。 然而，基于大语言模型的定理证明器大多只是寻找任何正确的证明，并在找到之后才提升其质量。 我们提出了 Lever，一种可将对正确证明的搜索目标进行编程化设置，并在搜索过程中对其进行优化的证明搜索算法。 Lever 在 AND/OR 证明图上对部分证明进行评分，将已实现的目标值与未完成的子目标的预测值相结合，从而在证明完成之前就让目标引导搜索过程。 同一机制还能优化计算成本、证明长度、主题不纯度，甚至它们的加权组合，而 Lean 内核则确保证明的正确性。 在 Lean 4 的 PutnamBench 测试中，在预算匹配的情况下，Lever 的成本比一个强大的单对话智能体低 34%（34\%），同时将解题率从 80%（80\%）提升至 96%（96\%）。 在降低主题不纯度方面（即证明偏离其定理主题的程度），Lever 优于事后重构方法（成本为后者的三分之二且效果更可靠，分别降低了 42%（42\%）和 33%（33\%））；而在证明长度这一重构方法所针对的指标上，Lever 的表现已接近后者。 通过调整目标函数的权重，可以描绘出质量与成本之间的权衡曲线，从而让用户能够选择更优质的证明究竟值多少代价。 总体而言，Lever 是一种性能卓越、成本高效且可调节的证明搜索算法，适用于在正确证明的空间中进行探索。

paragraphs.en: Mathematicians have long valued proofs for more than their correctness. A proof may be shorter, more elementary, or reveal structure that another proof obscures. The four-color theorem, for example, was proved in 1976 and formally verified decades later, yet a substantially different proof fifty years on exposed new structure in planar graphs and led to a near-linear-time coloring algorithm ( Appel and Haken, 1977 ; Gonthier, 2008 ; Inoue et al., 2026 ) . More broadly, the mathematical literature has debated the importance of characteristics like purity, simplicity and explanation ( Steiner, 1978 ; Detlefsen and Arana, 2011 ; Thiele, 2003 ; Tao, 2007 ) . The challenge is, therefore, not only to find a correct proof, but to choose among many.

paragraphs.en: This observation is crucial in the context of LLM-powered theorem provers that may generate correct proofs differing sharply in the computation needed to find them, their length, and the machinery they invoke. Yet current systems largely separate these concerns: proof search returns any verified proof ( NearAI, 2026 ; MistralAI, 2026 ; Rögnvaldsson et al., 2026 ) , sometimes with mechanisms to reduce inference cost, and proof quality is improved only afterwards through post-hoc refactoring ( Ahuja et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2026 ; Fu et al., 2026 ) . We take a different view: the objective over the space of proofs should be programmable, with correctness as a constraint . Optimizing such objectives during search can be both cheaper and more effective than optimizing it afterwards: a post-hoc method revisits a proof already paid for, and possibly inherits a trajectory (mathematical argument) chosen for a different objective.
paragraphs.zh: 在由大型语言模型（LLM）驱动的定理证明器中，这一观察结果至关重要。这些系统可能会生成正确的证明，但这些证明在所需计算量、长度以及所调用的机制方面可能存在显著差异。 然而，现有系统大多将这些关注点分离处理：证明搜索会返回任何经过验证的证明（NearAI, 2026；MistralAI, 2026；Rögnvaldsson 等, 2026），有时还会采用机制来降低推理成本，而证明质量的提升则仅在事后通过重构实现（Ahuja 等, 2024；Lu 等, 2026；Fu 等, 2026）。 我们持不同观点：在证明空间中，目标函数应当可编程，同时以正确性作为约束条件。 在搜索过程中优化此类目标函数，可能比事后优化更便宜且更有效：事后方法需要重新审视一个已经付出代价的证明，并可能继承为不同目标而选择的推理路径（数学论证）。

paragraphs.en: The key idea of Lever is to score a proof before it is finished. A partial proof has some goals proved and others still open. Lever scores it as the realized scored of the proved parts plus a predicted value for each open goal; at any time only the partial proof with the best score is expanded, so the objective steers search from the beginning rather than after the task is complete. We support this mechanism by representing partial proofs as an AND/OR graph: a theorem or a goal (OR node) is proved by any one of its alternative decompositions (AND nodes), and an argument needs all of its subgoals (OR nodes). We demonstrate that objectives such as computational cost, proof length or topical impurity, or a weighted sum of them compose over the proof graphs, allowing us to optimize them. In this process, correctness is never compromised: the Lean kernel checks every decomposition, and the assembled final proof.
paragraphs.zh: Lever 的核心思想是在证明完成之前对其打分。 一个部分证明包含一些已证明的目标，而另一些目标仍处于待解决状态。 Lever 的评分由已证明部分的实现得分与每个未解决目标的预测值之和构成；在任何时刻，只有得分最高的部分证明会被扩展，因此目标从一开始就引导搜索方向，而不是在任务完成后才进行引导。 我们通过将部分证明表示为 AND/OR 图来支持这一机制：一个定理或目标（OR 节点）可以通过其任意一种替代分解方式（AND 节点）得到证明，而一个论证则需要其所有子目标（OR 节点）均被满足。 我们证明了诸如计算成本、证明长度或主题不纯度等目标，或者这些目标的加权总和，可以作用于证明图之上，从而使我们能够对这些目标进行优化。 在此过程中，正确性从未受到任何影响：Lean 内核会检查每一种分解方式以及最终组合而成的完整证明。

paragraphs.en: On PutnamBench ( Tsoukalas et al., 2024 ) , with the same model and budget allocation as a strong agent that generates proofs in a single conversation, Lever raises the solve rate under a $3 budget from 80.0 % 80.0\% to 96.3 % 96.3\% while reducing average cost from $1.44 to $0.95, a 34 % 34\% reduction. The gain comes from keeping contexts local: Lever reads less than half the input tokens of the single-conversation agent. We then optimize the proof itself, for length and topical impurity , which we operationalize following work on purity of method ( Detlefsen and Arana, 2011 ; Martinot, 2024 ) : a proof accumulates impurity when it depends on results outside the subject of its theorem. So, length is often amenable to local compression, whereas purity can depend on the argument chosen at the start. Consistent with this, Lever approaches post-hoc refactoring on length, but outperforms both refactoring and direct instruction on impurity, at two-thirds of refactoring’s cost. Finally, varying the weight on quality metrics traces explicit quality–cost trade-off curves. This turns theorem proving from searching for any verified proof into searching for a verified proof under a user-specified objective, using the same search algorithm.

paragraphs.en: LLMs for theorem proving. LLM provers range from tactic generators inside tree search ( Polu and Sutskever, 2020 ; Yang et al., 2023 ; Xin et al., 2024 ; Xin et al., 2025 ) to whole-proof generators refined with compiler feedback ( First et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2025 ) . Decomposition has since become central: an informal draft becomes a formal sketch whose subgoals are proved separately ( Jiang et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024a ; Dong et al., 2024 ; Ren et al., 2025 ) , and agentic systems such as HILBERT ( Varambally et al., 2026 ) and Goedel-Architect ( Chung et al., 2026 ) complete these, while others learn from millions of attempts ( Chen et al., 2025 ; Achim et al., 2025 ; Hubert et al., 2025 ; Tsoukalas et al., 2026 ) ; LEAP ( Kung et al., 2026 ) maintains an AND/OR graph but explores it depth-first; all these systems search for any correct proof. On cost, Rögnvaldsson et al. (2026) decide when to restart from a new decomposition, and Quarry ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) ranks decompositions by predicted hammer solvability; in either case simple linear models with limited features from Lean structures make predictions. Proof quality is improved by refactoring a finished proof ( Ahuja et al., 2024 ; Gu et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026 ; Fu et al., 2026 ) . Lever instead lets an explicit objective over cost and proof quality steer the search using LLM-based value functions.

paragraphs.en: Value-guided search. AO ∗ finds the cheapest solution graph of an AND/OR graph under an admissible heuristic ( Martelli and Montanari, 1973 ; Nilsson, 2014 ) , with extensions to cyclic graphs ( Hansen and Zilberstein, 2001 ) and games ( Allis et al., 1994 ) . Learned values replaced hand-written heuristics in Monte Carlo tree search ( Kocsis and Szepesvári, 2006 ; Silver et al., 2016 ; Silver et al., 2018 ; Guez et al., 2018 ) and HyperTree Proof Search ( Lample et al., 2022 ) ; closest in spirit, Retro* ( Chen et al., 2020 ) learns the cost-to-go of AND/OR trees for retrosynthesis. LLM search over partial solutions ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Hao et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Snell et al., 2024 ) is typically guided by self-evaluation or process rewards that score correctness ( Lightman et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024b ) . Lever differs in three ways: its expansions are stochastic, so a goal can be redrawn; its priors learn from the draws already paid for; and its objective composes the remaining computational cost, the concern of rational metareasoning and costly search ( Russell and Wefald, 1991 ; Sabbata et al., 2025 ; Weitzman, 1979 ) , with arbitrary proof metrics.
paragraphs.zh: 价值引导搜索。 AO* 在可采纳启发式函数下，能够找到 AND/OR 图的最廉价解图（Martelli 和 Montanari，1973；Nilsson，2014），并扩展至循环图（Hansen 和 Zilberstein，2001）及博弈（Allis 等，1994）。 蒙特卡洛树搜索（Kocsis 和 Szepesvári，2006；Silver 等，2016；Silver 等，2018；Guez 等，2018）以及 HyperTree 证明搜索（Lample 等，2022）中，学习到的价值取代了手动编写的启发式函数；在理念上最接近的是 Retro*（Chen 等，2020），它通过反向合成学习 AND/OR 树的剩余成本。 LLM 对部分解的搜索（Yao 等，2023；Hao 等，2023；Zhou 等，2024；Snell 等，2024）通常由自我评估或过程奖励引导，这些奖励用于衡量正确性（Lightman 等，2023；Wang 等，2024b）。 Lever 在三个方面有所不同：其展开是随机的，因此目标可以被重新生成；其先验概率从已支付代价的抽取中学习；其目标函数整合了剩余的计算成本——这是理性元推理和昂贵搜索所关注的问题（Russell 和 Wefald，1991；Sabbata 等，2025；Weitzman，1979），并支持任意的证明度量标准。

paragraphs.en: 2. Expansion. An LLM expands each selected goal: it proposes a new decomposition (an AND node), the oracle checks it, and each subgoal it introduces is attached as a new OR node. paragraphs.en: Exactness under exact priors. With exact priors, the backed-up values are exact: for any nonnegative cost that adds along edges, V ⁡ ( n ) V(n) is the cost of the cheapest solution subgraph rooted at n n (counting a subgoal once per use), and V ⁡ ( n ) = ∞ V(n)=\infty exactly when none exists. We also share a formally verified proof of this in Lean (Appendix D ). Real value functions are noisy, which the update of Equation 1 and the margin δ \delta account for; their theoretical analysis is left for future work. When a subgoal is shared by several decompositions, paying for it once instead makes the cheapest solution subgraph NP-hard to find in general ( Sahni, 1974 ) ; Lever instead charges each shared subgoal to a single owner (Appendix A ).

paragraphs.en: Model and Pricing. We use DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 ( DeepSeek-AI et al., 2026 ) for every LLM call, in Lever and in all baselines, to match the baseline’s original setting. We price tokens at the official rates of $0.22, $0.007 and $0.66 per million input, cached input and output tokens ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) . Cost therefore depends heavily on the cache-hit rate. Served through multiple providers, API calls experience mean hit rate per call at 93.7% for NearAI (2026) , whose single long conversation re-reads its own history, and 86.2% for Lever , which starts many shorter conversations. To compare the searches rather than the caching, we fixed one 90% rate, between the two, before the evaluation runs. All costs in this paper are re-priced at this rate, and a problem counts as solved within a budget B B only if its re-priced cost is at most B B ; Appendix C.3 reports the observed costs.
paragraphs.zh: 模型与定价。 在 Lever 和所有基线模型中，我们每次调用 LLM 时都使用 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731（DeepSeek-AI 等，2026），以匹配基线模型的原始设置。 我们将令牌按官方费率定价：每百万输入令牌、缓存输入令牌和输出令牌分别收费 0.22 美元、0.007 美元和 0.66 美元（DeepSeek-AI，2026）。 因此，成本在很大程度上取决于缓存命中率。 由于通过多个提供商提供服务，API 调用的平均每次调用命中率为 NearAI（2026）的 93.7%——其单次长对话会重新读取自身历史记录——以及 Lever 的 86.2%——它会启动许多较短的对话。 为了比较搜索本身而非缓存效果，我们在评估运行前将命中率固定为两者之间的 90%。 本文中的所有成本均按此费率重新计算；一个问题仅当其重新计算后的成本不超过预算 B 时，才被视为在预算 B 内解决；附录 C.3 报告了观测到的成本。

paragraphs.en: Data. We use PutnamBench ( Tsoukalas et al., 2024 ) , originally containing 672 672 competition problems formalized in Lean 4 (v4.31.0). Most are easy for a strong agent, while the hardest can take days of repeated attempts, too long for controlled comparisons. Hence, we rank the problems by what the published run of NearAI (2026) spent to solve them and take ranks 51 51 – 150 150 , a slice that is hard but tractable; Appendix C.1 gives the full procedure and its biases. 20 20 of these calibrate the value functions (§ 4.4 ), and the other 80 80 form the evaluation set (§ 5 ).
paragraphs.zh: 数据。 我们使用 PutnamBench（Tsoukalas 等人，2024），其原始版本包含 672 个以 Lean 4（v4.31.0）形式化的竞赛问题。 其中大多数对强大的智能体而言较为简单，而最难的问题可能需要数日的反复尝试，时间过长，无法用于受控比较。 因此，我们根据 NearAI（2026）的公开运行版本解决这些问题所花费的时间对其进行排序，并选取第 51–150 名的问题，这一区间既具挑战性又可处理；附录 C.1 提供了完整流程及其偏差。其中 20 个问题用于校准价值函数（§4.4），其余 80 个问题构成评估集（§5）。

paragraphs.en: We discuss salient aspects of Lever ’s agent for goal expansion, leaving detailed descriptions in Appendix A .
paragraphs.zh: 我们讨论了 Lever 的智能体在目标扩展方面的关键特性，详细描述请参见附录 A。

paragraphs.en: Expanding a goal. Each expansion is one conversation of an LLM agent ( Yao et al., 2022 ) with a Lean workspace, with tools for Lean compilation ( Santos et al., 2025 ) , Mathlib retrieval ( Lu et al., 2025 ) , Python, and file I/O; it ends by submitting a file or reporting the goal false. To decompose a goal, the agent writes a Lean proof that relies on open subgoals; small lemmas are proved in place and larger ones are left open. Each open helper becomes a subgoal, to be closed in a future iteration. It annotates dependencies among open subgoals with the sorry_using tactic of LeanArchitect ( Zhu et al., 2026 ; Chung et al., 2026 ) , so that subgoals can share work. To prove a goal directly , the agent writes a complete proof with no open subgoals; § 5 states when this is enforced.
paragraphs.zh: 扩展目标。 每次扩展都是一个 LLM 智能体（Yao et al., 2022）与 Lean 工作区之间的对话，其中包含用于 Lean 编译的工具（Santos et al., 2025）、Mathlib 检索工具（Lu et al., 2025）、Python 以及文件 I/O；该过程最终以提交一个文件或报告目标为假而结束。 为了分解一个目标，智能体会编写一个依赖开放子目标的 Lean 证明；小型引理会当场被证明，而较大的引理则保持开放状态。 每个开放的辅助目标都会成为一个子目标，并在未来的迭代中被闭合。 它使用 LeanArchitect 的 sorry_using 战术（Zhu et al., 2026; Chung et al., 2026）来标注开放子目标之间的依赖关系，以便子目标可以共享工作成果。 为了直接证明一个目标，智能体会编写一个没有开放子目标的完整证明；§5 说明了在何种情况下会强制执行此操作。

paragraphs.en: Context. Before the search, a planner writes an informal proof of the problem, following Varambally et al. (2026) and Chung et al. (2026) . Every expansion carries this plan in its system prompt, and the planner’s cost is included in every cost we report for Lever . A subgoal’s conversation starts from its parent’s compacted output, or its full transcript if short, so the agent knows why the subgoal was introduced without carrying its parent’s work (Appendix A ). Every LLM inference call is made with 32 32 K completion tokens at temperature 1.0 1.0 ; planning with high-effort reasoning and expansion with low-effort reasoning.
paragraphs.zh: 背景。 在搜索之前，规划器会按照 Varambally 等人（2026）和 Chung 等人（2026）的方法，为问题撰写一份非正式证明。 每次扩展都会在其系统提示中包含该计划，并且规划器的成本会被计入我们为 Lever 报告的每一项成本中。 子目标的对话从其父节点的压缩输出开始；如果父节点输出较短，则从完整转录开始，这样智能体就能了解引入该子目标的原因，而无需重复父节点的工作（附录 A）。 每次 LLM 推理调用均使用 32,320 个完成令牌，温度设为 1.0；规划采用高努力推理，扩展则采用低努力推理。

paragraphs.en: Disproofs and soundness. The agent may report a goal false, with an informal reason (formal disproofs as in Lin et al. (2025) are not integrated for simplicity; these can wander into their own long trajectories). This ends the decomposition, and values are updated as in § 3.3 . When the root is solved, the solution subgraph is assembled into one Lean file and checked by the kernel. A problem counts as solved only if this file compiles using only the standard axioms, without sorry , admit , axiom or native_decide .
paragraphs.zh: 反证与正确性。智能体可能会报告某个目标为假，并给出一个非正式的理由（为简化起见，未集成如 Lin et al. (2025) 中的形式化反证；这些反证可能会演变为各自独立的长轨迹）。至此，分解过程结束，数值将按 § 3.3 中的方式更新。当根节点被解决后，解决方案子图将被整合为一个 Lean 文件，并由内核进行检查。只有当该文件仅使用标准公理进行编译，且未使用 sorry、admit、axiom 或 native_decide 时，问题才被视为已解决。

paragraphs.en: Correctness and computational cost. Correctness is enforced as a constraint: an unsolved goal costs ∞ \infty , so every objective is minimized over proofs that Lean type-checks. Computational cost, comp , is the dollars spent on LLM calls at the rates of § 4.1 . Spend already incurred cannot be recovered, so the search never optimizes it: each decision minimizes the remaining cost of finishing the proof, as estimated by the value function (§ 4.4 ), and every expansion replaces part of that estimate with what it actually cost (§ 3.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 正确性与计算成本。 正确性被作为约束强制执行：未解决的目标会耗费 ∞ \infty 的成本，因此所有目标都在 Lean 类型检查通过的证明中进行最小化。 计算成本 comp 是指在 § 4.1 所述费率下调用 LLM 所花费的费用。 已经产生的支出无法收回，因此搜索过程不会对其进行优化：每个决策都会最小化完成证明所需的剩余成本（由价值函数 (§ 4.4) 估计），而每次扩展则会用实际发生的成本取代该估计值的一部分 (§ 3.3)。

paragraphs.en: Topical impurity. ( imp ) instead measures the source of content in a proof. A proof is pure when it uses only what its theorem is about ( Detlefsen and Arana, 2011 ) . Purity is not computable in general, since a human must decide what a theorem’s content is ( Martinot, 2024 ) , so we read the content off Mathlib’s structure ( Community Mathlib, 2020 ) . Every library name has a namespace and a directory, e.g. , ZMod.wilsons_lemma is about ZMod and lives in Mathlib/NumberTheory . A theorem’s subject is the namespaces and directories of the names its statement uses. A referenced library theorem is impure when it falls outside the subject on both accounts; a generic lemma with no namespace, such as mul_pos , is impure only if it also lies outside a fixed set of infrastructure directories ( e.g. , Mathlib/Data/Nat ) that proofs of every topic use. Overall, we measure impurity as the number of impure references. See Figure 3 for an illustration of pure and impure proofs. We note here that this is a proxy for measuring mathematical (im)purity; further discussion and limitations of this metric are in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 主题不纯度。 （imp）实际上衡量的是证明中内容的来源。 当且仅当一个证明仅使用其定理所讨论的内容时，该证明才是纯的（Detlefsen 和 Arana，2011）。 一般而言，纯度是不可计算的，因为人类必须决定一个定理的内容是什么（Martinot，2024），因此我们从 Mathlib 的结构中读取内容（Community Mathlib，2020）。 每个库名都包含一个命名空间和一个目录，例如，ZMod.wilsons_lemma 与 ZMod 相关，并位于 Mathlib/NumberTheory 中。 一个定理的主题是其陈述所使用的名称所对应的命名空间和目录。 如果某个引用的库定理在这两个方面都超出了主题范围，则它是不纯的；而像 mul_pos 这样没有命名空间的通用引理，只有当它也位于所有主题证明都会使用的基础设施目录（例如 Mathlib/Data/Nat）的固定集合之外时，才被视为不纯。 总体而言，我们将不纯度衡量为不纯引用的数量。 关于纯证明和不纯证明的示例，请参见图 3。 我们在此指出，这仅是衡量数学（不）纯度的一个代理指标；对该指标的进一步讨论和局限性见附录 B。

paragraphs.en: Predicting comp and len . For comp and len , an LLM reads the open goal and picks one of seven bins on a log 2 \log_{2} scale ($0.016–$0.512 and 512–16,384 Lean tokens), and the goal is priced at its bin’s geometric center. Further, for len , the estimate is 0.2 0.2 times the bin’s center, deliberately underestimating length so that shorter proofs get explored. The prompt carries 40 40 in-context examples from offline runs on the calibration problems. Using an LLM as a value function prior is inexpensive: these calls make up only 0.89 % 0.89\% of Lever ’s spend, and are always included in the reported costs.

paragraphs.en: Predicting impurity. Impurity has a real floor, since a proof can cite nothing outside its subject, so the natural estimate for an open goal is 0 0 . In practice this made search unstable: every open goal looked pure, so redrawing always beat keeping a decomposition, and graphs grew huge. We instead score every open goal at a constant 4 4 references, the 25 25 th percentile of impurity over calibration goals.

paragraphs.en: Decomposition makes proof search cheaper. Table 1 compares the two systems at $3. Lever solves 96.3 % 96.3\% of the problems, against 80.0 % 80.0\% for NearAI, and costs 34 % 34\% less. This is not a trade-off between solving and saving: Lever does better on both . paragraphs.en: Identifying cheaper strategies. Lever ’s algorithm uses the value function to reject decompositions whose subgoals sum up to be more expensive than the goal itself, and draw a new decomposition. On putnam_1972_a3 , for example, Lever rejects its first decomposition from the value predictions alone, before working on any of its subgoals, and proves the theorem through a second decomposition predicted to be cheaper (Appendix C.4.1 ). However, such cases are rare, and not every redraw leads to savings: every subgraph that is given up on represents a sunk cost that is deducted from the global budget.
paragraphs.zh: 识别更便宜的策略。 Lever 的算法利用价值函数来拒绝那些子目标总和比目标本身更昂贵的分解，并绘制新的分解。 例如，在 putnam_1972_a3 中，Lever 仅根据价值预测就拒绝了其第一个分解，而尚未处理任何子目标，并通过一个预测为更便宜的第二个分解证明了该定理（附录 C.4.1）。 然而，这类情况很少见，而且并非每次重新绘制都能节省成本：每个放弃的子图都代表一项沉没成本，会从全局预算中扣除。

paragraphs.en: Baselines. Existing proof refactoring methods that target length, such as Lean Refactor ( Lu et al., 2026 ) and ProofOptimizer ( Gu et al., 2025 ) are not publicly available, while ImProver ( Ahuja et al., 2024 ) targets a much older Lean version (v4.9) and model; none can be run in our controlled setup, with the same model, Lean version and budget. To our knowledge, no existing method optimizes topical impurity, and none optimizes proof quality during search . We therefore build baselines atop the strong agent from NearAI (2026) . + Instruct steers the agent during its search: the end of its prompt states the metric and asks for a proof that minimizes it. + Refactor improves the proof after the search, as post-hoc refactoring does: it is handed NearAI’s finished baseline proof (§ 5.1 ) and asked to improve the proof. Together they cover the two alternatives to optimizing during search: steering by instruction and repairing afterwards. See Appendix C.5 for details.

paragraphs.en: Impurity optimization. We run Lever λ imp {}_{\texttt{imp}}^{\lambda} for λ ∈ { 0.01 , 0.1 } \lambda\in\{0.01,0.1\} with results in Figure 5 (left). Our + Refactor baseline reduces impurity by 33 % 33\% at $2.88 per problem. At λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 , Lever ’s proofs are 42 % 42\% purer, at $1.85, about two-thirds of + Refactor ’s cost. Lever is also more reliable: the standard deviation of its per-problem reduction is 32 32 points, against 101 101 for + Refactor , whose rewrites can backfire badly (on putnam_2007_a2 , from 29 29 out-of-subject references to 132 132 ). Instructing the agent to look for pure proofs does not help either: + Instruct ’s proofs are, on the contrary, 11 % 11\% less pure than the baseline, indicating that the agent loses context of the search objective in its single long session. This indicates that, when a metric depends on the proof strategy itself, optimizing it during search and treating it locally, works best.

paragraphs.en: Trade-offs among metrics. As shown in Figure 5 , Lever allows tracing a cost-quality trade-off curve: as λ \lambda rises, proof quality improves and the search costs more. Since λ \lambda is a conversion rate between metrics, a user can choose how much quality is worth paying for, and move smoothly along this frontier. In contrast, any fixed policy, such as the baselines considered here, admits only single points in this space. We observe that Lever ’s search also reveals relationships among various quality metrics (Table 2 ). Shortening a proof makes it purer: as proofs get shorter ( + 4 % → − 21 % +4\%\rightarrow-21\% ), impurity reduces as well ( + 1 % → − 18 % +1\%\rightarrow-18\% ). This is likely because as a proof is shortened, impure references are removed for free. However, the reverse does not hold: optimizing for impurity alone ( + 1 % → − 42 % +1\%\rightarrow-42\% ) makes proofs longer ( + 4 % → + 10 % +4\%\rightarrow+10\% ); this supports our observation that optimizing impurity requires a different strategy than what works for length reduction.

paragraphs.en: We presented Lever , a proof search algorithm that treats correctness as a constraint and makes the objective over correct proofs programmable. By valuing partial proofs over an AND/OR graph, combining realized costs with predictions for open goals, Lever optimizes that objective during search rather than repairing a proof afterwards. On PutnamBench, it is 34 % 34\% cheaper than a strong single-conversation agent while solving more problems ( 96 % 96\% against 80 % 80\% ). On topical impurity, search-time optimization removes more out-of-subject references than post-hoc refactoring at two-thirds of its cost, and on proof length it approaches refactoring. A single weight trades quality against cost, letting a user choose how much a better proof is worth.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 Lever，这是一种证明搜索算法，它将正确性视为一种约束，并使对正确证明的目标进行编程成为可能。 通过在 AND/OR 图中对部分证明进行估值，并将已实现的成本与开放目标的预测相结合，Lever 在搜索过程中优化该目标，而不是事后修复证明。 在 PutnamBench 上，它比强大的单对话智能体便宜 34%（34\%），同时能解决更多问题（96%（96\%）对 80%（80\%））。 在主题不纯度方面，搜索时间优化以三分之二的成本移除了比事后重构更多的非主题引用；在证明长度方面，其效果接近于重构。 单个权重在质量与成本之间进行权衡，让用户可以选择更优质的证明值多少钱。

paragraphs.en: Decomposing a goal. The agent writes the proof of the target in the file it is given, and may add two kinds of helper lemmas above it. Closed helpers are small steps proved in place. Open helpers are large steps left as sorry_using […] , where the list names the declarations in the file that the helper’s own proof will use; each becomes a subgoal, proved in a later conversation. Every declaration it adds carries a LeanArchitect blueprint attribute, an informal statement and proof in words, so a subgoal’s conversation knows what its lemma is for. A file is accepted only if its header, the declarations it was handed and the target’s signature are unchanged; the target is its last declaration, with no sorry in its body; every helper lemma is either proved or open with exactly sorry_using […] as its body; and it uses none of native_decide , axiom , admit , or search tactics ending in ? .
paragraphs.zh: 分解目标。 智能体将目标的证明写入其收到的文件中，并可以在其上方添加两种类型的辅助引理。 封闭辅助步骤是原地证明的小步骤。 开放辅助步骤是作为 sorry_using […] 保留的大步骤，其中列表指明了文件中该辅助步骤自身证明将使用的声明；每个声明都会成为一个子目标，并在后续对话中加以证明。 它添加的每个声明都带有 LeanArchitect 蓝图属性，即一个用文字表述的非正式陈述和证明，这样子目标的对话就能了解其引理的作用。 仅当文件的标题、其接收到的声明以及目标的签名未发生更改时，该文件才会被接受；目标是其最后一个声明，且其主体中不包含任何 sorry；每个辅助引理要么已被证明，要么以 exactly sorry_using […] 作为其主体保持开放状态；并且它不使用任何以 ? 结尾的 native_decide、axiom、admit 或 search 策略。

paragraphs.en: Shared subgoals. A subgoal’s identity is its Lean file with the blueprint annotations stripped: the lemma, together with the open helpers it depends on through sorry_using . Two decompositions that introduce the same lemma, or a subgoal whose proof uses a sibling it depends on, therefore reach the same OR node, which is proved once. A proof should then pay for a shared subgoal once, not once per use as the recursion of § 3.1 does, and under that accounting finding the cheapest solution subgraph is NP-hard ( Sahni, 1974 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 共享子目标。 一个子目标的身份由其 Lean 文件决定，其中蓝图注释已被移除：即该引理以及它通过 sorry_using 所依赖的开放辅助引理。 两个引入相同引理的分解，或一个其证明依赖于某个兄弟节点的子目标，都会到达同一个 OR 节点，而该节点只需被证明一次。 因此，在证明中，共享子目标应仅被计算一次，而非像 § 3.1 中的递归那样每次使用都单独计算；根据这种计算方式，寻找最便宜的解子图是 NP-难的（Sahni, 1974）。

paragraphs.en: Lever instead charges each shared subgoal to one goal, the one whose decomposition first introduced it (or the next, if that decomposition dies). Every alternative decomposition of that goal pays for the subgoal, not only the one that introduced it, so the goal compares its alternatives on what each would cost; decompositions of other goals use the subgoal free, since it is proved once for all of them. Ownership depends only on the order in which nodes were created, not on which alternatives are chosen, so values cannot oscillate; the cost is that a shared subgoal’s price drops out of the root’s value when its owner chooses an alternative that does not use it.
paragraphs.zh: 相反，Lever 将每个共享子目标归因于一个目标，即最初通过分解引入该子目标的目标（如果该分解终止，则归因于下一个目标）。 对该目标的每种替代分解都需要为此子目标付费，而不仅仅是引入它的分解；因此，该目标会依据各替代方案的成本进行比较；其他目标的分解可免费使用此子目标，因为它的证明对所有目标而言都是一次性的。 所有权仅取决于节点的创建顺序，而非所选的替代方案，因此数值不会发生振荡；其代价是，当子目标的所有者选择一个不使用它的替代方案时，该共享子目标的价格会从根节点的值中扣除。

paragraphs.en: Context inheritance. A subgoal’s conversation starts from its parent’s: from the full transcript if the parent’s conversation is under 20 20 K tokens, and otherwise from the parent’s compacted output. Any conversation that reaches 128 128 K tokens is likewise replaced by its compacted output.

paragraphs.en: Disproofs and failures. A disproof is a claim about the goal rather than the attempt: the goal is closed as false, its value becomes ∞ \infty , and later decompositions of its parent are told the statement is false and why. An attempt that ends without an accepted file is a failure. Its spend is charged, and its goal’s estimate rises by one σ \sigma (§ 3.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 反证与失败。 反证是对目标而非尝试的断言：该目标被判定为假，其值变为 ∞ \infty ，之后对其父节点的分解过程会被告知该陈述为假及其原因。 未生成任何被接受文件的尝试即为失败。 其消耗会被计收，且其目标的估计值将上升一个 σ \sigma (§ 3.3)。

paragraphs.en: Can the metric be gamed? A proof could lower its count by re-proving an out-of-subject library lemma as a local helper: the helper’s statement names only definitions, which are not charged, and its proof may cite nothing impure. We checked for this on the 20 20 problems of § 5.2 , counting the helpers whose statements name something outside the subject. At λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 , Lever writes more helpers than at λ = 0 \lambda=0 ( 36.1 36.1 against 25.9 25.9 per proof), but only slightly more off-subject ones ( 11.2 11.2 against 10.1 10.1 ; NearAI: 14.1 14.1 ). Charging every off-subject helper as one more impure reference lowers Lever ’s mean impurity reduction at λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 by under one point.
paragraphs.zh: 这个指标能否被操纵？ 一种证明方法可以通过将某个非主题领域的库引理重新证明为局部辅助引理来降低其计数：该辅助引理的陈述仅提及定义（这些定义不计费），且其证明不得引用任何不纯内容。 我们在 §5.2 的 20×20 个问题中对此进行了检查，统计了那些陈述中提及主题领域以外内容的辅助引理数量。 在 λ = 0.1 时，Lever 编写的辅助引理比 λ = 0 时更多（每证明 36.1 个，对比 25.9 个），但非主题领域的辅助引理仅略多（11.2 个，对比 10.1 个；NearAI：14.1 个）。 将每个非主题领域的辅助引理计为一次额外的不纯引用，会使 Lever 在 λ = 0.1 时的平均不纯度降低幅度不足一点。

paragraphs.en: Limitations. Topical impurity is a proxy for purity of method. It takes Mathlib’s organization as a stand-in for mathematical subject, and namespace and directory boundaries do not always match a mathematician’s; the infrastructure set is a judgment, measured on one pilot corpus. It counts references rather than weighing them, so an essential detour through another field counts the same as a routine lemma from it. And, as above, it charges a local re-proof of an out-of-subject lemma only through the library theorems that re-proof cites.
paragraphs.zh: 局限性。 主题不纯度是方法纯度的代理指标。 它将 Mathlib 的组织结构视为数学学科的代表，但命名空间和目录边界并不总能与数学家的划分一致；所设定的基础设施是一种判断，其衡量依据仅来自一个试点语料库。 它统计引用次数而非评估其权重，因此，必须经过另一个领域的重要绕路，其计数与从该领域引用的常规引理相同。 并且，如上文所述，对于跨学科引理的局部重新证明，它仅通过被该重新证明所引用的库定理来计费。

paragraphs.en: We rank PutnamBench with the published run of NearAI (2026) , which solves all 672 672 problems and records every attempt’s tokens and wall-clock time. Each problem is ranked by the token cost of its cheapest solving attempt, most expensive first, priced at a fixed rate table of $0.15, $0.003 and $0.60 per million input, cached input and output tokens (prices from NearAI (2026) originally; these rates are no longer available). Most problems are easy for this agent: below rank 150 150 , the median problem is solved in 0.3 0.3 hours (Table 3 ). The hardest are impractical for controlled comparisons that run every method on every problem: in the top 50 50 , 20 20 problems needed more than one attempt and one took 5.5 5.5 days. We therefore take ranks 51 51 – 150 150 , hard for the agent but solved in a median of 1.5 1.5 hours, and split them at random into 20 20 calibration and 80 80 evaluation problems.

paragraphs.en: + Refactor starts from NearAI’s finished proof of the problem (§ 5.1 ), which replaces the statement in the agent’s workspace, and is asked to rewrite it for the objective while keeping it a proof of the same theorem. Its objective adds what Lever tells a redraw about the attempt in hand: for impurity, how many times the proof leaves the subject and which lemmas do, grouped by field; for length, the proof’s token count. paragraphs.zh: + 重构从 NearAI 对问题的已完成证明（§ 5.1）开始，该证明会替换智能体工作区中的陈述，并被要求围绕目标对其进行重写，同时保持其为同一定理的证明。 其目标补充了 Lever 在关于当前尝试的重新绘制中所说明的内容：对于不纯度，即证明脱离主题的次数以及哪些引理脱离了主题，并按领域分组；对于长度，即证明的令牌数量。 此次运行的上限为 $4.5 减去 NearAI 运行所花费的成本，这样整个流程的预算就与其他所有方法相同，且其报告的成本也包含了 NearAI 的成本。
